title: cue-switchboard-labs-journal
content:
Purpose: quick personal lab for the 'switchboard' approach — route an instruction through multiple micro-templates and use lightweight adjudication to reduce hallucination and instruction drift. Notes to self: this is messy; keep small experiments, capture failure modes, pick 2-3 bench tasks (summarize, classify, extract).

High-level idea:
- Given user instruction + doc/context, run N template variants in parallel (N=3-5). Each variant focuses on a different anchor: literal-extractive, narrative-summary, structured-bullet.
- Add a short verifier probe prompting the model to assert confidence and list evidence spans.
- Adjudicator: simple majority on content overlap OR prefer variant with evidence span that maps to input tokens.

Quick templates (WORKING):
T1 — Extractive anchor:
  "Answer succinctly using only the text below. If not present, say 'Not stated'. Provide the span(s) you used."
T2 — Summarize-as-narrative:
  "Write a short narrative summary (2-3 sentences). Then bullet 3 supporting facts and their sentence numbers from the text."
T3 — Structured-field:
  "Return JSON with keys: \"role\", \"action\", \"deadline\". If unknown, use null. After JSON, list supporting lines."

Few-shot exemplars (for summarization):
EX1 input: paragraph about release cadence -> summary: "We plan monthly minor releases..." -> evidence: "(lines 2-3)"
EX2 input: customer complaint snippet -> summary + bullets -> evidence lines
(keep examples terse; reuse small tokens)

Adjudication heuristics (proto):
- If >1 variant returns same top-level fact -> accept.
- If only one variant has explicit evidence spans -> accept that one.
- If contradictions -> fall back to safe response: "I don't have enough information to answer confidently."

Observed failure cases (notes):
- Role-bleed: when system instruction defines persona, some variants over-interpret (T2 becomes creative). Need hard guard: "Do not add content beyond input."
- Span drift: model returns evidence but it doesn't map to literal tokens (paraphrase mismatch). Consider asking for character indices or quoting spans.
- Token budget explosion: running 4 variants + verifier is expensive for long docs. Try prefix-sampling (send only top-k sentences by BM25) as a prefilter.
- Anchor bias: extractive template tends to return 'Not stated' too often; it misses implied facts. Maybe add soft inference rule.

Experiments to run (priority):
1) Summarization on 300 short docs, compare single-template baseline vs switchboard ensemble. Metrics: hallucination rate (manual spot check), ROUGE, evidence-match (automated).
2) Structured extraction for SLA fields (role/action/deadline) on 200 docs. Verify adjudication success rate.
3) Ablation: verifier ON/OFF to see change in hallucination.

Scratch outputs (examples from quick runs):
- Input: "Datacenter X will migrate on 2025-04-01; contact ops-team."
  T1 -> {deadline: "2025-04-01", role: "datacenter ops", action: "migrate"} evidence: "line1"
  T2 -> narrative adds: "planned to complete by EOD" (halluc) evidence: "(none)"
  Adjudicator -> picks T1, returns T1 JSON + note: "T2 added unsupported completion claim"

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to encode confidence scores reliably? Use model-provided probabilities? (costly). Maybe a heuristic: length of evidence spans + explicit 'I am X% confident' token.
- Should the adjudicator be another model call or deterministic overlap? Tradeoffs between latency and correctness.
- Integrate with prefix selection: experiment with BM25 vs rouge-L prefilter.
- Add negative exemplars to few-shot sets (examples that show hallucination) — good teaching signal.

Experiment schedule (quick):
- Week 1: build lightweight harness (local runner), run N=3 variants on 200 docs (summaries + extraction).
- Week 2: add verifier pass and simple adjudicator logic. Run A/B.
- Week 3: analyze failure cases, refine templates, collect ~50 manual checks.

Notes to self: keep prompts short and reductive; avoid multi-turn teaching inside template. Try to capture span as literal quote where possible ("quote the exact span"). Link to GH PR for runner: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-router/pull/42 — adjust CLI flags to support --variants and --evidence-output.

Random musings (ideas):
- Could use a cheap model for adjudication (small L1) while the main responses come from L2 to save cost. Need to test bias.
- Consider a fallback policy for 'critical' customers: if adjudication fails, automatically route to human-in-loop (SLA gating).

Wrap-up: rough, hungry for iteration. Capture failures aggressively. When I get manual labels, convert common hallucination patterns to training negatives for future model fine-tune.

--- end of current scratch lab notes (Aisha)
